parsed.explanation: The division adds a tier-1 universal exposure: from 1 July 2026 criminalizing restroom/changing-room use by birth sex in government buildings AND all public-facing private businesses (gas stations, restaurants, venues, hospitals), misdemeanour up to one year, with litigation pending and no demonstrated remedy. One documented arrest ended in 24 hours in a men's ward. The parent regime compounds this: federal sex-binary passport policy upheld Nov 2025 with travellers stranded, federal facility bans, documented federal corrections hormone-hair conversion policy, documented immigration-custody beatings/sexual abuse of trans detainees, hostile counterterrorism framing, and allied-government travel advisories. No documented trans-specific violence above background and no organized sweeps keep it above the 0.25 tier, but criminalized daily presence plus state custody harm place it below the 0.35 anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order bars self-selected gender on passports/visas; X-marker processing halted Feb 2025; Supreme Court allowed restriction Nov 2025; trans travellers report passports confiscated or blocked and being stranded abroad. Visa officers instructed to refuse where doubt about sex exists, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered.
entry_documents.protection: Pre-2025 X-marker passports remain valid to expiration; the foreign-ministry policy is still challenged in national courts; a legal-aid organisation runs a running documentation FAQ.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate into refusal, fraud allegation, then immigration detention — where custody abuse is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: A trans woman was arrested 19 March 2025 under a state bathroom law and held 24 hours in a men's ward. Federal corrections adopted a conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026 and stopped counting trans prisoners. Trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; a suit challenges the division law; a September 2024 ruling nullified a state hormone ban for prisoners.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility criminalisation plus document mismatch raises the odds any stop becomes a detention in birth-sex placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law criminalizes birth-sex-mismatched facility use in government buildings and public-facing private businesses including hospitals, up to one year jail — the only such law reaching private businesses, with steeper penalties than peers. Parent map: facility bans across many states/provinces; 4 states make it a criminal offence; another state's arrest is documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Suit filed 30 April 2026 by six residents before effect; 29 states/provinces plus 4 units and the capital district have no mapped ban; one state still issues X licences.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor cannot avoid the reach: restaurants, gas stations and hospitals are covered; private inclusivity cannot shield against statute.

care_services.exposure: Hospitals are covered by the division's criminal facility law, so emergency admission risks exposure. Gender-affirming care is banned for minors in 27 states; an Oct 2025 rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients; DOJ subpoenaed over 20 hospitals for under-19 patient records.
care_services.protection: Not documented for visitors: no shown emergency-care safeguard, medication-continuation guarantee or insurance waiver for trans travellers.
care_services.interaction: A medical emergency outs the traveller; a travelling minor on treatment may be denied care; record subpoenas amplify data exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders describe youth care as 'mutilation' and direct investigation of 'gender ideology'; DOJ reward memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy flag 'radically pro-transgender' ideology; advocates compare trajectory to early genocide stages. Polls: 66% back ASAB document mandates, 69% back athlete bans.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several executive orders blocked or enjoined; employment discrimination barred nationally since 2020.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both outing probability and the severity of any official encounter.

minors_guardians.exposure: March 2026 division law forces schools, childcare and medical professionals to disclose a trans minor's status to parents within three days; federal order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; under-19 medical records subpoenaed; care bans in 27 states affect a travelling minor's treatment.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented: no shown shield for visiting families; a 2022 exile-for-care felony bill was blocked, but later bills advanced.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's outing can become a data or care event; a parent's support does not prevent mandated disclosure or record collection.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific data showing trans violence above the general homicide rate was identified — thin, not safe. National risk assessment flagged 4 states as 'Do Not Travel' for trans people; eight-plus allied governments issued travel advisories over document and data rules. Bias against sexual orientation runs one-seventh to one-fifth of reported hate incidents.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute; police/courts function and several orders are enjoined; 23 states cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Advisories reflect document and facility exposure more than street violence, which remains undocumented rather than absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Outcome of the division suit, any 16 June 2026 judicial narrowing, and enforcement frequency are unknown; classification of the offence (misdemeanour vs felony) is disputed; no enforcement record exists yet; only 22 states plus the capital district bar gender-identity discrimination; passport litigation unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active, funded litigation with named plaintiffs; legal-aid FAQ; multiple national orders blocked or enjoined; prior civil-rights wins with fee awards show courts sometimes rule for trans claimants.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper and pending recourse cannot be relied on mid-trip; the exposure operates now while remedies are contingent.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Veluna restricts toilets in public buildings with no offence of being trans and a polite public. Here facility use is itself criminal in government AND private businesses including hospitals, an arrest with men's-ward detention is documented, federal documents cannot be made to match, and federal custody carries documented abuse. Recourse in both is weak; the exposures here are broader and more severe.

Roughly comparable, marginally higher: Savorek pairs universal birth-sex facility and ward rules with recurring police stops and fraud-threat extortion. This division matches the facility and ward exposure and adds a criminal penalty up to a year plus federal custody abuse, but lacks a documented police-stop/extortion pattern and retains active pre-effect litigation and states with no bans.

Materially lower than 0.55-B: Teravi's harms are refusals by ferries and guesthouses partly remedied by mediators, with a conviction and no facility mandate. Here the state itself criminalizes everyday facility use covering hospitals, documents cannot be corrected federally, and custody abuse is documented — tier-1 and tier-2 exposures that local hospitality and partial remedies cannot offset.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a nested exposure. The parent supplies documents that cannot be made to match (X markers ended, sex-binary passports upheld Nov 2025, travellers stranded), federal facility exclusions, a conversion-style corrections policy, and documented immigration-custody abuse of trans detainees — reachable by a visitor through any visa or document discrepancy. The division then adds the country's only criminal bathroom statute reaching private businesses, including hospitals, effective 1 July 2026, with one documented arrest ending in a men's ward and no established remedy. Official counterterrorism framing and majority public support for restrictions raise outing and encounter severity, while a travelling minor faces mandated disclosure, record subpoenas and care bans. Active litigation, a national hate-crime statute, functioning courts that have occasionally ruled for trans claimants, and absence of documented trans-specific violence above background keep this above the organized-targeting tier — but tier-1 universal criminalization with contingent recourse governs.
